meta.description: Designs genomics experiments so technical nuisance variation (batch, lane, plate, flow cell, operator, reagent lot, processing day) is balanced against the biological variable of interest and therefore estimable rather than confounded, using constrained sample-to-batch assignment (designit, OSAT), the confounder/mediator/collider distinction, and the principle that no post-hoc correction recovers a fully confounded design. Covers detecting hidden batches with surrogate variable analysis, a decision table for downstream correction (ComBat-seq, RUVSeq, SVA) whose execution is deferred to differential-expression/batch-correction, and reproducibility metadata. Use when assigning samples to sequencing batches/lanes/plates, avoiding batch-condition confounding, deciding whether a design is salvageable by correction, choosing a correction method, or estimating the number of hidden batches. For the experimental unit, randomization, and blocking concepts see experimental-design/randomization-blocking.
meta.audit_type: re-audit after fix (fixes/bio-experimental-design-batch-design.md, commit e543a0a); 5 pre-fix inputs re-run as regression + 2 new inputs targeting the fix's own claims

scientific_integrity.detail: All numbers this session come from runs on labelled synthetic data (designs, matrices, the shared synthetic MaxQuant proteinGroups.txt); no fabricated DOIs/PMIDs/statistics; the eight references are unchanged from the pre-fix audit and were already confirmed real.

practice_boundaries.detail: Design/QC guidance only; no individual-level diagnostic or treatment content.

methodological_ground.detail: Core claims reproduced: confounded design is unrescuable (ComBat errors or zeroes out the effect), unbalanced ComBat inflates realized FDR to 33.1% vs 4.6% with batch in the model, SVA recovers a hidden batch (cor=1.00), and the new verification step is a real confounding gate, not cosmetic.

code_usability.detail: All 7 inputs ran to completion on designit 0.5.0 / sva 3.54.0 / limma 3.62.2 with no syntax errors, missing dependencies, or infinite loops. (Inputs 6 and 7's first drafts had bugs in this auditor's own test harness -- a stale variable and an unfiltered NaN aggregation -- not in the Skill's code; both were fixed and re-run, see run/ scripts and eval_viewer.)

functional_suitability.note: Completeness improved: the new Reference/Bridge Channel Layout section gives real designit code where none existed pre-fix. Still no OSAT code despite OSAT being named as an alternative. Correctness 4/4 equivalent: every tested claim reproduced. Appropriateness improved: TMT/proteomics now has real code, not just a taxonomy row.

reliability.note: Major gain: the SVA block no longer crashes unexplained on NA (confirmed, Input 4) and the post-optimization verification is a real, confirmed gate (Input 1, Input 6). Docked because the fix is not fully consistent: the bridge-channel block inherited the hard stopifnot(all(tab>0)) confounding check but NOT the primary block's soft imbalance() warning, and Input 2 shows exactly that gap firing silently on a real imbalance of 3.

agent_usability.note: The pre-fix gap ('no instruction to verify the condition x batch table after optimization') is fixed and confirmed to work for the primary assignment path; clear causal framing retained.

human_usability.note: Unaffected by the fix; natural trigger language retained.

key_strengths: The P1 SVA/NA crash is fully fixed and confirmed by execution: the block now messages the missing-value fraction, filters to 738/1500 complete features exactly matching an independent recount, and recovers the hidden day effect (cor(SV1, day)=1.00) instead of crashing unexplained.

The fixer's own caveat -- that complete-case filtering biases surrogate variables toward abundant, well-detected features -- is empirically true on real data: complete features are 1.78 log2 units more abundant (p=3.7e-69) and detected in a median of 8/8 vs 6/8 samples.

The new post-optimization verification is a real gate, not decorative: it halted on every genuinely confounded layout tested (primary batch and bridge-plex) and did not false-positive on a balanced one.

The new bridge/reference-channel section provides real, runnable designit code where the pre-fix Skill had none, and correctly reserves the pooled-reference position in every plex (15/15/15/15, channel 16 always empty).
All three original findings (P1 SVA crash, P2 no verification, P2 no bridge code) are addressed with working code; only one narrow gap remains (below).

recommendations.title: Bridge-channel block doesn't inherit the soft imbalance warning
recommendations.problem: The Reference/Bridge Channel Layout section copies the primary block's hard stopifnot(all(tab>0)) confounding check but not its soft imbalance() warning. Input 2's optimizer converged to case 8/8/8/6, ctrl 7/7/7/9 (cell spread 3) with no warning -- the same 'suboptimal split accepted silently' failure mode the original P2 finding described, now recurring in the new bridge code path.
recommendations.root_cause: The bridge section was written by copying only the hard-fail line ('same confounding check as above') and not the adjacent soft-warning block from the primary assignment section.
recommendations.fix: Add the same `imbalance <- max(tab) - min(tab); if (imbalance > 1) warning(...)` block to the Reference/Bridge Channel Layout section, immediately after its `stopifnot(all(tab > 0))` line.

recommendations.title: Balance-verification code shown only for the primary condition, not other covariates
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's prose says to repeat the table/stopifnot check for every balanced covariate (e.g. sex), but the shown code block only demonstrates it for condition.
recommendations.root_cause: One worked example, not a loop over covariates.
recommendations.fix: Show the loop explicitly, e.g. `for (v in c('condition','sex')) { tab <- table(assignment[[v]], assignment$batch); stopifnot(all(tab > 0)) }`.
